paper.title: Spatial structure often inhibits the evolution of cooperation in the snowdrift game

headline: Hauert-Doebeli 2004 spatial snowdrift (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; worst inhibition gap 0.173 at r*=0.7 (replicator) vs best-takes-over gap 0.001; replicator f_lat(0.8)=0.000 (extinct) vs best-takes-over 0.334

verdicts.gate: P1 well-mixed reproduces interior ESS f=1-r (|f_wm-(1-r)|<=0.03; slope in [-1.1,-0.9])
P2 spatial structure INHIBITS cooperation (exists r* in [0.3,0.7] with (1-r*)-f_lat>=0.10; f_lat<1-r for a majority)
P3 high-r extinction on the lattice (f_lat(0.8)<=0.05 while f_wm(0.8)>=0.15; gap>=0.10)

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the counter-intuitive spatial INHIBITION of cooperation in the snowdrift game, prove it is specific to the stochastic replicator rule (the best-takes-over gate), and would catch a mislabeled Nowak-May

citations: Hauert, C. & Doebeli, M. (2004). Spatial structure often inhibits the evolution of cooperation in the snowdrift game. Nature 428:643-646. doi:10.1038/nature02360.
Nowak, M.A. & May, R.M. (1992). Evolutionary games and spatial chaos. Nature 359:826-829.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the steady-state cooperator fraction f_lat vs the well-mixed ESS 1-r, with a best-takes-over control as the mechanism-specificity gate
